market.summary: A French-language PMB pilot anchored in ENSEA and BNCI remains the strongest family opportunity; COBES-CI/AUF provide coordination leverage. One actual CNDJ public book-title query succeeded after partial network recovery. National/public-reading, university, specialist and cultural priorities remain substantial; most live checks were blocked by environment-wide proxy failures, and Goethe blocks automated paths. No national market share or largest-ten ranking is established.
market.platform_strategy: First verify ENSEA and BNCI PMB; then CERAP and UAO routes through official discovery. PMB requires deployment-specific adapter development/validation: the existing app implementation is pinned to known sites, not a universal configuration switch. Koha is a secondary candidate via Goethe Abidjan and scoped university survey evidence; reusing its adapter still requires a real allowed search. UVCI/Invenio-style repository and ScholarVox/Cairn/Onleihe digital entitlements must be separate from physical holdings. Recovery confirms live ENSEA PMB copy-level parsing and a separate Bibliosoft JSON API at IFCI. Treat Bibliosoft as a custom adapter candidate, not PMB. INP-HB portal is digital-only reserve evidence.

limitations: Four observed book-search responses across institutions: three substantial selected targets (CNDJ exact-title, ENSEA exact-main-title, IFCI broad token-related titles) plus one digital-only INP-HB reserve. Seven further selected successes remain unmet. Transport incidents, robots exclusion, unresolved routes and one zero-result university test constrain verification; no countrywide outage conclusion.
No national largest-ten ranking established. Priorities use dissimilar, dated/undated collection totals, subset totals, seats and institutional/network proxies; they are not comparable rankings.

Only actual live returned books are counted. IFCI does not prove Le petit prince held: broad query returned related tokens and strict query0. INP-HB digital links are not physical holdings. Indexed BNCI/ESATIC records remain discovery evidence only.

HTTP503 never clears robots. Goethe’s wildcard Disallow:/ was respected. CERAP’s official public-IP catalogue origin timed out at robots. No authentication, private-IP probe, TLS bypass, challenge bypass, outreach or product changes.
Web discovery sometimes serves cached/indexed excerpts. Their retrieval date does not establish current holdings, exact publication date, or live endpoint operation.
Public catalogue access does not establish borrowing eligibility. IFCI explicitly requires membership; CERAP lists subscription fees; university and CNDJ access need separate verification.
Older country overviews saying no public-library network conflict with current official CLAC evidence; current official sources are preferred.
PMB/Koha/ISIS-family presence does not establish current public search, interoperability or nationwide adoption shares.

Shared control evidence: ../country-context/reachability-control.json and ../country-context/client-comparison.json. Other origins showed identical proxy503; partial recovery of example.com did not establish catalog reachability.

IFCI public API exposes numberOfCopies=0 in bibliographic summaries but getCopies returned1 copy; copy flags are observed response fields, not independently validated circulation. Unnecessary staff-account metadata and nonvisible text were redacted from saved evidence.
Original08:24–08:30 failures are preserved under historical_probe_failures/evidence; recovery requests were one fresh robots preflight per target, followed by bounded allowed public searches.
